**How to use this file:** The cross-project snapshot, read cold by every agent on the Light startup cascade. **It is a SNAPSHOT, not a log — each update *replaces* the previous state.** Shipped history lives in each repo's `CHANGELOG.md` + `docs/deploy-log.md`; per-session narrative lives in the handoff docs. Refreshed at `#lock` by whoever is active.

**Do not edit this file without Justin's approval.** Propose changes; don't make them directly.

**Keep it lean — target ~50 lines of body.** If a project needs more than a few lines, the detail belongs in that repo's own sprint or build doc, not here. **When something ships, it moves *out* of here.**

> ### 🔴 WHY THIS FILE KEEPS TURNING INTO A LOG — read this before you edit it
>
> **On 2026-08-11 this file was 152 lines against a 50-line target, and ONE line of it was 6,902 characters carrying 11 dated appendages from 10 different instances.** The obvious explanation — *"replacing is hard, so under time pressure everyone appends"* — **does not survive contact with the artifact.** Those appendages were *more* work than an in-place edit: every one was signed with an instance name and a full ISO timestamp, several carried explicit ownership routing, and one said outright that it was recorded here **because the working doc that held it was being retired and there was nowhere else.** That is the signature of *correspondence*, not of a shortcut.
>
> **⇒ The real mechanism: this is the only broadcast channel that exists.** There is no live AC↔AC delivery; Slack reaches only Justin; a lane brief reaches only its own lane. **This file is the one document every instance loads at startup** — so it is structurally the only way to reach *everyone*, and a broadcast bus is append-only by nature, because **you cannot "replace" someone else's message.** The snapshot and the bus were two different documents sharing one filename.
>
> **⇒ So the bus now has its own bounded home: the 📮 BULLETIN at the bottom.** Put cross-lane notices there, not in the body. **The body is a snapshot and gets replaced; the bulletin is a queue and gets drained.** *(Diagnosed 2026-08-11.)*

> ### 📦 What this file deliberately does NOT record — go ask the repo
>
> **Anything git answers better, because a doc can never be more current than the repo it describes.** No commit SHAs, no branch lists, no worktree inventories, no test counts. Those went stale here repeatedly and *looked authoritative while doing it*.
>
> ```bash
> git -C <repo> log --oneline -1 main     # what main actually is
> git -C <repo> status --porcelain        # uncommitted work, other agents included
> git -C <repo> worktree list             # who else is standing in this repo
> git -C <repo> rev-list --count origin/main..main   # unpushed commits
> ```
>
> **If you feel the urge to write repo state into this file, that urge is the smell.** It belongs in the command above, in its Step, or in its Gate.

> # 📁 `docs/working/` IS RETIRED. EVERYTHING IS IN `docs/sessions/` NOW.
>
> **One folder, not two.** Working docs and session docs were always the same thing, so they now live in one place. **Completed 2026-09-02: 58 files → 0.**
>
> ### 🔎 CAN'T FIND A DOC? SEARCH BY ITS NAME. Nobody needs to fix the link.
>
> 🔑 **A document's FILENAME NEVER CHANGES. Retiring it moves it; it does not rename it.** ⇒ **So any path you meet — however stale — still tells you the one thing you need: what the file is called.**
>
> ```bash
> git ls-files "*2026.07.15-ac3-step78-real-health-design*"
> ```
>
> **That finds it wherever it lives, in one command, forever.** It is somewhere under **`docs/sessions/`** — at the top level if live, in **`docs/sessions/historical/YYYY.MM/`** if retired — **but you do not need to know which, and you should not spend a thought on it.**
>
> ⭐ **Why by NAME and not by date, even though the date is right there in the filename:** a date lookup asks you to reconstruct a path, and it fails on every edge — a doc filed in the wrong month, a doc with no date prefix, or any future change to how `historical/` is organised. ⚠️ **And it fails SILENTLY: you look, find nothing, and conclude the document is gone.** **A name search has none of those failure modes.**
>
> ### 🔴 THE RULE THAT MATTERS MOST: DO NOT FIX REFERENCES TO SESSION DOCS.
>
> **A stale path to a session doc is not a bug, and NOBODY GOES LOOKING FOR THEM.** The filename is stable forever, so one name search finds the file no matter how old the path is. **Sweeping for them is make-work, and the make-work was bad enough to have consumed whole sessions.**
>
> ⭐ **But if you happen to be in a doc and see a session path that has moved, fix it.** **What is abolished is the OBLIGATION TO SWEEP — not the permission to fix what is already under your nose.**
>
> ⚠️ **This does NOT extend to source-of-truth docs** — protocols, manuals, ADRs, ARCHITECTURE, the Hub, sprint docs. **Those still get their references fixed when they move**, because they are cited as authority rather than as history.
>
> 📌 **ARCHIVING SOMETHING YOURSELF? Two rules, in `lock-protocol.md` step 10: never change the filename, and file it under the DOC'S OWN date — never the month you happen to be archiving in.** *(Twelve docs were misfiled the second way before it was written down.)*

> **This section exists because appending is legitimate and the body is not the place for it** (see the diagnosis at the top). **Rules, all three load-bearing:**
> 1. **Every entry starts `**[YYYY-MM-DD · instance]**`.** No date, no entry.
> 2. **Drained at every `#lock`.** 🔴 **THE ONLY QUESTION IS: *DOES THIS NEED TO STAY?*** *(Justin, 2026-09-02.)* **If it is stale and its substance is already persisted somewhere durable — DELETE IT.** **If it's stale but *hasn't* properly been persisted, persist it properly.** **If deleting it would lose live, in-flight information, keep it.** ⇒ **Anything still true gets folded into the body above first, then the entry is deleted.**
>    - 🔴 **DELETE MEANS DELETE. Do NOT leave a `[DRAINED]` tombstone behind.** *(Justin, 2026-09-02: **"do we want to have endless drained notes? Doesn't that defeat the purpose?"**)* **Tombstones were a habit that grew up against this rule, and several had accumulated — turning a queue into a second dumping ground, which is the exact failure this section was built to end.**
>    - ⭐ **The journey belongs in `CHANGELOG.md`, which every AC already reads on load, and the full text is in git history regardless.** ⇒ **Memorialize in the changelog FIRST, then delete — never point at an entry that does not exist yet.**
> 3. 🔴 **An entry more than 7 days old is OVERDUE BY DEFINITION.** The dates are the staleness signal, and they work whether or not anyone remembers to drain — **a bulletin carrying an old entry is telling you the drain has not run.** That is the point: this fails *loudly* rather than accumulating quietly, which is exactly what the body did for eleven entries.
> 4. **Keep entries short and route-shaped** — what changed, who owns the residue. Substance goes in the owning doc; this is the pointer that gets it read.
